questions.question: What happens when R reads `x <- 5; if (x = 0) { "zero" } else { "other" }`, where a single `=` was typed in the condition?
options: R sets `x` to 0 and returns `"zero"`, since the assignment succeeds
R sets `x` to 0 and returns `"other"`, since the value 0 counts as `FALSE`
R rejects the line with a syntax error, since `=` assigns and does not compare
R compares `x` with 0 and returns `"other"`, since `=` means `==` inside `if`

questions.question: In a script run at the top level, an `if` block ends with a closing brace `}` on its own line, and the next line starts with `else { ... }`. What happens when the script runs?
options: R stops at `else` with a syntax error, since the statement already ended at `}`
R joins the two lines and runs the `if`–`else` statement as intended
R runs the `if` block and silently skips the `else` block in every case
R treats the `else` block as an extra block that runs in every case

questions.question: What does R return for `x <- 15; if (x > 5) { "over 5" } else if (x > 10) { "over 10" } else { "at most 5" }`?
What happens when R runs `x <- c(3, NA, 8); if (x[2] > 5) { "big" } else { "small" }`?
options: the error `missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed`

questions.question: In R 4.3, what happens when R runs `x <- c(-1, 4); if (x > 0) { "pos" } else { "neg" }`?
What does R print for the last line of `x <- 2; y <- 10; if (x > 5) { y <- 0 }; y`?
options: an error, as the `if` has no `else` block

questions.question: What does R print for the last line of `x <- -3; y <- if (x > 0) x^2 else -x; y`?
options: an error, as `if` cannot appear on the right of `<-`

questions.question: What does R return for `age <- 17; member <- TRUE; if (age >= 18 && member) { "full" } else if (member) { "junior" } else { "guest" }`?
After running `x <- 5; y <- 0; if (x > 0) { if (x > 10) { y <- 2 } else { y <- 1 } }`, which value does `y` hold?
options: an error, as an `if` cannot contain another `if`

questions.question: Which value does `x` hold after R runs `x <- 3; if (x > 2) { x <- x - 2 } else { x <- x + 10 }`?
options: an error, as a block may not change the object in its condition

questions.question: A numeric vector `x` holds several values. Which condition makes `if (...) { msg <- "check data" }` run its block exactly when at least one element of `x` is negative?
For a single number `x`, which definition computes $f(x)=x+1$ for $x<0$ and $f(x)=x^2$ for $x\ge 0$?
What does R print for the last line of `x <- c(5, -2, 0); s <- 0; for (v in x) { if (v > 0) { s <- s + v } else if (v < 0) { s <- s - v } }; s`?
options: an error, since `0` matches none of the blocks

questions.question: What does R print for the last line of `x <- 15; y <- "none"; if (x > 5) { y <- "over 5" }; if (x > 10) { y <- "over 10" }; y`?
What does R print for the last line of `x <- -1; y <- 0; z <- 0; if (x > 0) y <- 1; z <- 2; c(y, z)`, in which the `if` has no braces?
options: an error, since the `if` has no braces

questions.question: A filter found nothing, so `x <- c(2, 7)[c(2, 7) > 10]` is empty. What happens when R then runs `if (x > 0) { "pos" } else { "none" }`?
options: the error `argument is of length zero`

questions.question: For a single number `x <- -4`, `if (x >= 0) sqrt(x) else NA` returns `NA` without a warning, while `ifelse(x >= 0, sqrt(x), NA)` for the vector `x <- c(4, -4)` warns `NaNs produced`. What explains the difference?
options: `if` suppresses every warning raised inside its blocks
`sqrt()` warns only when it receives a vector longer than 1
`if` runs one block; `ifelse()` computes `sqrt(x)` in full
`if` replaces the negative number by `NA` before `sqrt()` sees it

questions.question: For `x <- NA`, which condition makes `if (...) "positive" else "other"` return `[1] "other"` instead of stopping with an error?
What does R return for `x <- 5; z <- NA; if (x > 0) { "a" } else if (z > 0) { "b" } else { "c" }`?
options: the error `missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed`

questions.question: The chain `if (x < 0) { "low" } else if (x >= 0 && x <= 2) { "mid" } else { "high" }` labels a single number `x`. Which shorter chain returns the same label for every non-missing number `x`?
